name: immersive-controls
summary: Controls shown over content that fills the screen (a book's page, a photo, a video, a map): a bar at the top and a bar at the foot, laid over the content, which never moves for them.

properties.name: presented
properties.description: Whether the bars show. The app turns it on and off, usually on a tap in the middle of the content.

slots.name: top
slots.description: The top bar's controls, such as Close at the leading end and one action at the trailing end. It stands in the status bar's band, beside any camera housing.

slots.name: bottom
slots.description: The bottom bar's controls, such as a scrubber and a group of actions. It stands in the home indicator's band, across the width under any housing.

states.name: rest
states.description: Hidden: the content alone fills the screen. Presented: both bars over the content, each slid in from its own edge, or faded in under reduced motion, and the content where it was, unscaled and undimmed.

accessibility.name: Each bar's controls are named by their own labels; the bars add no name of their own.
accessibility.keyboard: The bars' controls follow the content in the tab order while presented, and leave it when hidden.
accessibility.web: Two fixed-position toolbars (role="toolbar", named by the app) over the content, which keeps its own layout; hidden ones are removed, not only made transparent.
accessibility.apple: An overlay on the content: VoiceOver reads the top bar's controls, then the bottom bar's, and the content under them is still reachable.
accessibility.windows: Two overlaid panels of controls on the content, each a UI Automation group, removed from the tree when hidden.

cases.person: A picture that fills the screen, where it was before the tap; Close and Share float at the top corners in the status band, and Edit and Favourite float along the foot, each in a glass capsule.
The picture alone, filling the screen, in the same place.

deviations: A browser reports no camera housing, so web's bars stand in env(safe-area-inset-*) and the page's own margins.
Each bar is one Liquid Glass container on iOS 26 and later, so its pieces of glass blend as the system's toolbars do; the app draws its controls in squircle glass shapes.
Reads the camera housing from reservedRegions(kind: .occlusion) on iOS 27.1 and later; an app can pass its own occlusions and safe area.
A desktop window has no status or home-indicator band, so the bars stand a gap in from the window's edges.
